'''Joshua Dominique Powell''' (born January 25, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and coach. Powell won two NBA championships with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2009 and 2010, and has also spent time with the [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Atlanta Hawks]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Golden State Warriors]] and [[Houston Rockets]]. In 2013, Powell was a member of the [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] side that won the [[EuroLeague]] championship. He has also played in Russia, Italy, Argentina, Puerto Rico, China, the Philippines, Australia and Venezuela.

==College career==
Powell spent two years at [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|North Carolina State]], where in his freshman campaign, he averaged 7.2 points and 3.9 rebounds per game en route to earning a spot on the ACC All-Rookie squad. He went on to average 12.4 points and 5.3 rebounds in 31 games his sophomore season, and was named the team's most improved player as the recipient of the Tom Gugliotta Award. He ranked seventh in the ACC in blocks (1.3), 20th in scoring and 18th in rebounding. He was named to the All-ACC Tournament first team after putting up 20.0 points, 7.0 rebounds and 3.0 blocks in three contests, including a career-best 26-point effort in the championship game against [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.nba.com/player/#!/2694/|title=Josh Powell|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 7, 2016|archive-date=April 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160401124428/http://stats.nba.com/player/#!/2694/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Early years===
After going undrafted in the [[2003 NBA draft]], Powell spent the preseason with the [[Dallas Mavericks]], before moving to Russia for his first professional season. He managed just two games for [[PBC Lokomotiv-Rostov|Lokomotiv-Rostov]] before joining Italian team [[Scafati Basket]] for the rest of the 2003–04 season. Following his stint in Italy, he returned to the United States and played for the Southern Crescent Lightning, helping them win the 2004 [[World Basketball Association|WBA]] championship. He also spent the 2004–05 season in Italy with [[JuveCaserta Basket]] before re-joining the Southern Crescent Lightning in 2005.

===Dallas Mavericks===
Powell re-signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in August 2005, but managed just 16 games over the first half of the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]]. On February 27, 2006, he was assigned to the [[Fort Worth Flyers]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. He was recalled by the Mavericks on March 4, and went on to play in 21 games throughout March and April. On April 4, 2006, he scored a season-high 12 points in a 127–101 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260404006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161018222940/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260404006|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 18, 2016|title=Mavericks put emphatic end to Kings' run of good defense|work=ESPN.com|date=April 4, 2006|access-date=October 17, 2016}}</ref> He finished the regular season with an 11-point, nine-rebound effort against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on April 19.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/poweljo01/gamelog/2006/|title=Josh Powell 2005-06 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=October 17, 2016}}</ref> The Mavericks reached the [[2006 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] in 2006, where they were defeated 4–2 by the [[Miami Heat]]. Powell appeared in six games over the Mavericks' playoff run.

===Indiana Pacers and Golden State Warriors===
In July 2006, Powell was traded, along with [[Darrell Armstrong]] and [[Rawle Marshall]], to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for [[Anthony Johnson (basketball)|Anthony Johnson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2006-07-23-mavs-pacers-trade_x.htm|title=Indiana acquires Armstrong, trades Johnson in deal with Mavericks|work=USAToday.com|date=July 23, 2006|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref> He appeared in just seven games for the Pacers in [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07]] before being traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in an eight-player deal on January 17, 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/trade_070117.html|title=PACERS MAKE 8-PLAYER TRADE WITH WARRIORS|work=NBA.com|date=January 17, 2007|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref> On January 27, 2007, in just his second game for the Warriors, Powell scored a then career-high 13 points in a 131–105 win over the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270127009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161018205735/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270127009|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 18, 2016|title=Warriors spread the wealth to win second straight|work=ESPN.com|date=January 27, 2007|access-date=October 17, 2016}}</ref> He played in 30 regular season games for the Warriors, as well as making four playoff appearances.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/poweljo01/gamelog/2007/|title=Josh Powell 2006-07 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=October 17, 2016}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers===
On August 14, 2007, Powell signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/jpowell_070814.html|title=Clippers Sign Forward Josh Powell|work=NBA.com|date=August 14, 2007|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref> On April 3, 2008, he recorded a career-high 13 rebounds in a 110–98 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280403023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161013221208/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280403023|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 13, 2016|title=Martin pours in 26 as Kings overcome last-place Clips|work=ESPN.com|date=April 3, 2008|access-date=October 13, 2016}}</ref> Three days later, he scored a career-high 22 points in a 105–79 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280406012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161014060240/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280406012|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 14, 2016|title=Rockets spread ball, handle Clippers to wrap up playoff berth|work=ESPN.com|date=April 6, 2008|access-date=October 13, 2016}}</ref> On July 30, 2008, he was waived by the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/news/Clippers_JoshPowell_080730.html|title=Clippers Waive Josh Powell|work=NBA.com|date=July 30, 2008|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers===
On August 14, 2008, Powell signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/080814joshpowell.html|title=LAKERS SIGN JOSH POWELL|work=NBA.com|date=August 14, 2008|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref> Over two seasons with the Lakers, he won two [[List of NBA champions|NBA championships]].

===Atlanta Hawks===
On July 26, 2010, Powell signed a one-year, $1.1 million contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Powell_Signs_072610.html|title=Hawks Sign F/C Josh Powell|work=NBA.com|date=July 26, 2010|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=McMenamin|first=Dave|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5412630|title=Powell signs with Hawks|work=ESPN.com|date=July 26, 2010|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref>

===China, Switzerland and Puerto Rico===
In September 2011, Powell signed with the [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]] for the [[2011–12 CBA season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/88303/josh-powell-moves-to-liaoning.html|title=Josh Powell moves to Liaoning|work=Sportando.com|date=September 5, 2011|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref> Following the CBA season, he joined [[Union Neuchâtel Basket]] for their Swiss Cup semi-final game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/other-leagues/90444/josh-powell-signs-with-neuchatel.html|title=Josh Powell signs with Neuchatel|work=Sportando.com|date=February 27, 2012|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/other-leagues/90513/swiss-team-neuchatel-tab-josh-powell-and-tajuan-porter.html|title=Swiss team Neuchatel tab Josh Powell and Tajuan Porter|work=Sportando.com|date=February 29, 2012|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rts.ch/sport/basketball/3825000-une-star-de-nba-evoluera-a-neuchatel-le-temps-dun-weekend.html|title=Une star de NBA évoluera à Neuchâtel le temps d'un week-end|work=rts.ch|date=March 2, 2012|access-date=October 7, 2016|language=fr}}</ref>

On March 29, 2012, Powell signed with Puerto Rican team [[Brujos de Guayama]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/91131/josh-powell-officially-signs-with-brujos-de-guayama.html|title=Josh Powell officially signs with Brujos de Guayama|work=Sportando.com|date=March 29, 2012|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref> Exactly one month later, he was replaced in the line-up by [[Marcus Fizer]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/91613/marcus-fizer-replaces-josh-powell-in-brujos-de-guayama.html|title=Marcus Fizer replaces Josh Powell in Brujos de Guayama|work=Sportando.com|date=April 29, 2012|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs===
On September 27, 2012, Powell signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for training camp.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/120927_training_camp|title=Spurs Add Four to Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2012|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref> He was later waived by the Spurs on October 26, 2012, after appearing in six preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/121026_powell|title=Spurs Waive Josh Powell|work=NBA.com|date=October 26, 2012|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref>

===Olympiacos===
On November 2, 2012, Powell signed with Greek team [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/96223/josh-powell-inks-with-olympiacos.html|title=Josh Powell inks with Olympiacos|work=Sportando.com|date=November 2, 2012|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref> He went on to help the team win the [[2012–13 Euroleague|2012–13 EuroLeague]] championship.

===New York Knicks===
On September 30, 2013, Powell signed with the [[New York Knicks]] for training camp.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://knicksnow.com/posts/3942/knicks-sign-josh-powell-and-justin-brownlee |title=Knicks Sign Josh Powell And Justin Brownlee |work=KnicksNow.com |date=September 30, 2013 |access-date=September 18, 2015 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005001803/http://knicksnow.com/posts/3942/knicks-sign-josh-powell-and-justin-brownlee#.V_d2QyN94zY |archive-date=October 5, 2013 }}</ref> He was later waived by the Knicks on October 25, 2013, after appearing in five preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14639|title=Knicks waive Ike Diogu, C.J. Leslie, Josh Powell, Jeremy Tyler, Chris Douglas-Roberts|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 25, 2013|access-date=September 18, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029184157/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14639|archive-date=October 29, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===China and the Philippines===
On October 30, 2013, Powell signed with the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] for the [[2013–14 CBA season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/107544/josh-powell-signs-in-china-with-guangdong.html|title=Josh Powell signs in China with Guangdong|work=Sportando.com|date=October 30, 2013|access-date=September 18, 2015}}</ref>

On April 1, 2014, Powell joined the [[Barangay Ginebra San Miguel]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]], one day before making his [[2014 PBA Commissioner's Cup|Commissioner's Cup]] debut.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lopez|first=Joshua|url=http://www.interaksyon.com/interaktv/new-import-josh-powell-compares-ginebra-to-his-old-la-lakers-team|title=New import Josh Powell compares Ginebra to his old LA Lakers team|work=InterAksyon.com|date=April 1, 2014|access-date=October 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161009140126/http://www.interaksyon.com/interaktv/new-import-josh-powell-compares-ginebra-to-his-old-la-lakers-team|archive-date=October 9, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Dy|first=Richard|url=http://www.spin.ph/sports/basketball/news/new-import-josh-powell-vows-to-bring-former-teammate-kobe-bryants-kill-mentality-to-ginebra|title=New import Josh Powell vows to bring former teammate Kobe Bryant's 'kill mentality' to Ginebra|work=Spin.ph|date=April 1, 2014|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref> He parted ways with Ginebra on April 13, 2014, after receiving an NBA call-up.<ref>{{cite web|last=Joble|first=Rey|url=http://www.interaksyon.com/interaktv/import-josh-powell-leaving-ginebra-to-sign-with-nbas-houston-rockets|title=Import Josh Powell leaving Ginebra to sign with NBA's Houston Rockets|work=InterAksyon.com|date=April 13, 2014|access-date=October 7, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161009143200/http://www.interaksyon.com/interaktv/import-josh-powell-leaving-ginebra-to-sign-with-nbas-houston-rockets|archive-date=October 9, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Dy|first=Richard|url=http://www.spin.ph/sports/basketball/news/ginebra-orphaned-as-import-josh-powell-gets-call-up-from-houston-rockets-in-time-for-nba-playoffs-v02|title=Ginebra orphaned as import Josh Powell gets call-up from Houston Rockets in time for NBA playoffs|work=Spin.ph|date=April 13, 2014|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref>

===Houston Rockets and Milwaukee Bucks===
On April 16, 2014, Powell signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-josh-powell|title=Rockets Sign Josh Powell|work=NBA.com|date=April 16, 2014|access-date=September 18, 2015}}</ref> On October 24, 2014, he was waived by the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-claim-earl-clark-waivers-and-request-waivers-josh-powell|title=Rockets Claim Earl Clark Off Waivers and Request Waivers on Josh Powell|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2014|access-date=September 18, 2015}}</ref> After being waived by the Rockets, Powell joined [[Kevin McHale (basketball)|Kevin McHale]]'s staff as a player development coach for the [[2014–15 Houston Rockets season|2014–15 season]].<ref name="bucks" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/141835/josh-powell-joins-rockets-coaching-staff.html|title=Josh Powell joins Rockets coaching staff|work=Sportando.com|date=November 20, 2014|access-date=September 18, 2015}}</ref>

On September 18, 2015, Powell signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for training camp.<ref name=bucks>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-announce-2015-training-camp-roster|title=BUCKS ANNOUNCE 2015 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|work=NBA.com|date=September 18, 2015|access-date=September 18, 2015}}</ref> He was later waived by the Bucks on October 21, 2015, after appearing in four preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-request-waivers-three-players|title=BUCKS REQUEST WAIVERS ON THREE PLAYERS|work=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2015|access-date=October 21, 2015}}</ref>

===Argentina, Puerto Rico and China===
On December 3, 2015, Powell signed with [[San Lorenzo de Almagro (basketball)|San Lorenzo de Almagro]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Básquet]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/183813/josh-powell-signs-in-argentina-with-san-lorenzo.html|title=Josh Powell signs in Argentina with San Lorenzo|work=Sportando.com|date=December 3, 2015|access-date=December 3, 2015}}</ref> In March 2016, he parted ways with San Lorenzo and signed with Puerto Rican team [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Fuentes|first=Christian|url=http://www.metro.pr/metrosport/powell-reforzara-a-los-indios/pGXpcB!aPlYW8KFLwqg/|title=Powell reforzará a los Indios|work=Metro.pr|date=March 28, 2016|access-date=March 28, 2016|language=es}}</ref>

On May 23, 2016, Powell signed with Luoyang Zhonghe of the Chinese [[National Basketball League (China)|NBL]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/200281/josh-powell-and-joe-jackson-sign-with-luoyang.html|title=Josh Powell and Joe Jackson sign with Luoyang|work=Sportando.com|date=May 24, 2016|access-date=May 30, 2016}}</ref>

===Sydney Kings===
On October 7, 2016, Powell signed with the [[Sydney Kings]] for the [[2016–17 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sydneykings.com/team-news/kings-sign-2-time-nba-champ/|title=KINGS SIGN 2-TIME NBA CHAMP|work=SydneyKings.com|date=October 7, 2016|access-date=October 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161009135856/http://www.sydneykings.com/team-news/kings-sign-2-time-nba-champ/|archive-date=October 9, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Uluc|first=Olgun|url=http://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/sydney-kings-sign-twotime-nba-champion-josh-powell-to-fulfil-teams-third-and-final-import-spot/news-story/c68b21ed002922a692e244584db38d72|title=Sydney Kings sign two-time NBA champion Josh Powell to fill team's third and final import spot|work=FoxSports.com.au|date=October 7, 2016|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref> Six days later, he made his debut for the Kings in their second game of the season. In 22½ minutes off the bench, he recorded 14 points and six rebounds in an 88–84 win over the [[Illawarra Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/backcourt-stars-shoot-kings-first-win/|title=BACKCOURT STARS SHOOT KINGS TO FIRST WIN|work=NBL.com.au|date=October 13, 2016|access-date=October 13, 2016|archive-date=October 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161013130247/http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/backcourt-stars-shoot-kings-first-win/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On October 20, he scored 17 points on 8-of-11 shooting off the bench in a 92–78 win over the [[New Zealand Breakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/impressive-kings-go-top-nz-win/|title=IMPRESSIVE KINGS GO TOP WITH NZ WIN|work=NBL.com.au|date=October 20, 2016|access-date=October 20, 2016|archive-date=October 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161021005304/http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/impressive-kings-go-top-nz-win/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 23, he scored a season-high 21 points in an 87–75 loss to Illawarra, dropping the Kings to 10–10 on the season with a fourth-straight defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/forman-ends-funk-hawks-keep-rolling/|title=FORMAN ENDS FUNK, HAWKS KEEP ROLLING|work=NBL.com.au|date=December 23, 2016|access-date=December 23, 2016|archive-date=December 24, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161224030810/http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/forman-ends-funk-hawks-keep-rolling/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Kings went on to finish the season in seventh place, missing the playoffs with a 13–15 record. In 27 games for the Kings, Powell averaged 9.4 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game.

===Venezuela and Korea===
On March 13, 2017, Powell signed with [[Trotamundos de Carabobo]] of the [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.caraotadigital.net/deportes/trotamundos-anuncio-la-llegada-de-un-ex-nba/|title=Trotamundos anunció la llegada de un ex NBA|work=caraotadigital.net|date=March 13, 2017|access-date=March 13, 2017|language=es}}{{Dead link|date=July 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> In October 2017, he joined [[Changwon LG Sakers]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]]. He left the team in November 2017 after appearing in nine games.
